actually, one of the advantages of sexual reproduction is diversity. Think of it this way- if you have a population of single celled organisms that reproduce exclusively asexually, they pass on 100% of their genes to their 'offspring'. This is good, because organisms 'want' to propagate their genome. However, the only way to add diversity to the population is through random mutation. Barring mutation, all 'offspring' of a parent with an ABC allele will be ABC. Think again of a population that is exactly the same as the first, except they reproduce sexually. During sexual reproduction, the genome is "shuffled"; parents with ABC alleles and abc alleles can produce gametes with ABC, abc, aBC, AbC... and so on. Though this method of reproduction does not pass on ALL genetic info to offspring, it is "good enough" and also offers the advantage of diversifying the population. This way, when a disease, famine, stressor etc comes around and kills all organisms with ABC, diversity in the population will 'save' those with the 'shuffled' genes. yeah idk where i was going with this but basically there are evolutionary advantages to both sexual and asexual reproduction but the fact that humans reproduce sexually shows that at some point in our lineage it was advantageous for us to shuffle the genome around.
